- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.3), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment or price; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak if sentiment remains bullish.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model fails to correct; reduce forecast slope or add downward bias in second half.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period price (last 7–10 days); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for final 7–10 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3), model often overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average or reduce volatility.
